subject: general
question: In an examination 80% students passed in Physics, 70% passed in Chemistry while 15% students failed in both subjects. If 325 students passed in both the subjects, find the total number of students who appeared in the examination.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Percentage of students passed in both = Passed in Physics + Passed in Chemistry + Failed in both − 100%

⇒ Passed in both = 80% + 70% + 15% − 100% = 65%

⇒ 65% of total students = 325

⇒ Total students = (325 ÷ 65) × 100 = 500

**∴ The correct answer is 500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Passed in Physics = 80%

Passed in Chemistry = 70%

Failed in both = 15%

Number of students passed in both = 325

 
 Total Students = 100%
 Failed in Both = 15%

 
 

 Physics (80%)
 Chemistry (70%)

 15%
 65%
 5%
 (Both)

**Formula Used:**

n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B)

Passed in at least one subject = 100% − Failed in both

**Calculations:**

⇒ Students passed in at least one subject = 100% − 15% = 85%

⇒ Let students passed in both subjects be x%.

⇒ 85% = 80% + 70% − x%

⇒ x% = 150% − 85% = 65%

⇒ Now, 65% of total students = 325

⇒ Total students = (325 ÷ 65) × 100

⇒ Total students = 5 × 100 = 500

**∴ The correct answer is 500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Venn Diagram Basics

The Universal Set represents 100% of the population. Any overlapping region represents elements common to both sets, also known as the intersection.

Two Sets Formula

n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B), where n(A ∪ B) is the total number of distinct elements in at least one of the sets.

Three Sets Formula

n(A ∪ B ∪ C) = n(A) + n(B) + n(C) − n(A ∩ B) − n(B ∩ C) − n(C ∩ A) + n(A ∩ B ∩ C).
